learning_objective: 🎯 Let us go on a journey to see how everyday objects like clothes, pots, and paper are created from nature!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Clothes do not grow on trees! We get soft cotton balls from cotton plants, spin them into long threads, and weave them together on machines to make the colorful shirts we wear.
A potter uses soft, wet earth called clay to make beautiful pots. They spin the clay on a special wheel, shape it with their hands, and bake it in an oven to make it hard.
Did you know paper comes from trees? Wood from trees is chopped up and mixed with water to make a soft paste called pulp, which is pressed flat and dried to make paper.

fun_activity.title: 🎨 My Shirt's Secret Tag!
fun_activity.instructions: Look inside the collar of your favorite t-shirt and find the little tag. Ask an adult to help you read it to see what material your shirt is made of, like cotton or polyester!

quick_recap: ⭐ We use threads from plants and animals to weave clothes.
⭐ Potters shape wet clay on a wheel and bake it to make strong pots.
⭐ We must save paper because it is made by cutting down real trees.
